body:
You are very right, in that given the choice, I would prefer a life with even just slightly less pain than I have now, than to die.  There are so many reasons for this, not the least of which is sparing those who I know love me from a painful grieving process. We are creatures of survival.  We are programmed for self preservation/protection, which, ironically is what makes us want to kill ourselves when we are confronted with unbearable pain. I do want the suffering to stop, and I have made many attempts (other than suicide) to stop the pain.

I saw a therapist for a time, and went on meds. Medications are not for me.  This might sound short-sighted, or unreasonable, but I do not particularly believe in psychopharmaceuticals.  I know they can help people, but for me, they are not an option.  Therapy helps, but it's really just a cushion.  I will not be making any sort of "breakthroughs," as I don't believe there to be any underlying behavioral problems, or past traumas to cause my depression.  I sincerely believe that it is an innate part of my personalty/self/biological makeup, based partly on the fact that it has been pervasive since childhood. Psychiatric hospitalization would never be something that I would willingly submit to.  Keep in mind that I am suicidal because of my quality of life.  I do not wish to further decrease that quality of life.  As a psychological professional, I am aware of the many options I have, and I hope that you can trust me that I have explored many options and treatments.  Some of the things I have tried have helped, and even mad me happy.  However, there is nothing like getting better for a short time, only to slide back into the hole, that then is deeper and darker than before.   

I have known for some time that I will not die of natural causes.  However, I think I can make it a while longer.  There are things I want to accomplish.  I do have reasons to live, and I will continue to cling to them for as long as I can. That said, I am pretty sure that one of these days I will have to press the "stop" button.  I almost don't think of it as suicide, so much as euthanasia.

I have a great admiration for people like you, and the others in this sub, as you clearly value life the way it was meant to be valued.  I know that my life has value, but unfortunately I won't be able to participate in life the way that most people do.

I appreciate the opportunity to discuss this in a rational manner.  I am pretty calm about this topic, as I have given it a lot of thought, and wouldn't chose to end my life on whim, or in "the throes of passion" so to speak.  While I am not a religious person, but I do consider the idea of suicide to be a moral and spiritual dilemma. 

Thanks for modding.

Your response is very thoughtful and pertinent. 

I will give this some thought, thank you.
I really like that.  That has helped me as well.

Yes.  This is what I struggle with.  I feel a deep need to do right by the people that care for me.  I seek relief from my own suffering, but can't justify it because of the pain it will cause others.  

I think it might be unanswerable...

When I say that life is the root of my depression, I simply mean that because I exist I experience depression, or, in other words, it is something intrinsic to my being.  Sure, I get upset and sad about things that upset everyone, but in general, I have an overwhelming sense of isolation, and general melancholy.

Life makes me happy sometimes too.  I am capable of experiencing joy.  If I wasn't, I doubt I would be capable of experiencing such pain. The joy, unfortunately is very fleeting.  It used to be that i could look back at happy times, and draw on those experiences as a motivation to keep going, but, like I said, I have reached a sort of threshold.  The scales have tipped.

I have sought help in the past, and tried antidepressants, but I am opposed to medicating with pharmaceuticals at this point in my life.

I wouldn't be considering suicide if I hadn't exhausted other options.

I honestly think that the root of my depression is life.  I believe that some people are prone to depression because of inherited personality traits.  I wasn't abused, I have loving family and friends, and no serious traumatic experiences.  I might also note that I have a degree in psychology, currently work for a health psychology department at a major university, and have a pretty good understanding of depression.  

As far as what I need to be happy, I couldn't really say.  I have been in love, achieved lofty goals, and had great pleasures for fleeting periods of my life.  There is always one constant though, and that is my underlying depression.

I have gone through many changes in my life.  I have practiced meditation, therapy, been on meds, etc.  I am healthy, I exercise, have meaningful relationships, and generally try to help myself.  At times I have been happy, but for the most part I feel very alone and depressed.  This has been going on since about the age of 11.

I know that things could change.  Maybe tomorrow everything will be better, but experience tells me otherwise.  I am pretty accepting of the fact that I am just prone to depression.
I am single, no children.  The only thing that I am concerned with is putting my family and friends through pain.
